Hon'ble Dinesh Kumar Singh,J.
1.
The present revision petition has been filed challenging the judgment and order dated 18.01.2008 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.5, Barabanki in Criminal Appeal No.77 of 1999.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge, Court No.5, Barabanki
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The appellate Court has dismissed the appeal filed by the revisionist against the judgment and order of conviction dated 30.11.1999 under Section 7(1) read with 16(1)(a)(1)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.
2. Learned Trial Court convicted the accused for the aforesaid offence and sentenced him to undergo 6 years rigorous imprisonment with fine of Rs.1,000/-.
The Appellate Court has dismissed the appeal vide impugned judgment and order.

3. Prosecution story, as per record, is that on 26.09.1986 at around 2:00 P.M., Food Inspector, Y.B.
Singh collected a sample of Paan Masala manufactured by Chaurasiya and sons, Masakganj,
Lucknow weighting 100 gms each from the grocery shop of the accused after giving purchase price Ram Lal vs State Of U.P. on 30 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120366653/
1 of Rs.6/-.

entities.text: Ram Lal vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Public analyst in his examination found that catechu and peppermint were missing from the sample while those were showing as ingredients of the substance by the manufacturer.
On the basis of the report of the public analyst, the revisionist was convicted by the trial Court and the same has been affirmed by the appellate court.
5. Learned counsel for the revisionist, Mr. Santosh Srivastava submits that the case is of the year 1986.
The revisionist had a Kirana shop and he was not the manufacturer of pan masala.
He was only a retailer where he sold many grocery items including pan masala.

He further submits that the revisionist has already undergone three months imprisonment and he is ready and willing to deposit the fine as directed by the trial Court and affirmed by the appellate Court.

6. Considering the substance of the allegation and the fact that the incident is of 1986 and the revisionist has already undergone three months imprisonment, this revision petition is disposed of by affirming the conviction but reducing the sentence to the sentence already undergone with a direction to the revisionist to deposit a fine of Rs.1,000/- within a period of three months from today.
